mainEntity.name: How do I know what size heater I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Measure your sauna's length, width and height in feet and multiply them to get cubic feet, then pick a heater whose range covers that number. Add volume for glass walls or doors. Every heater page lists the room range for each kW output, or send us your measurements and we'll recommend one.

mainEntity.name: Electric or wood-burning: what's the difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: Electric heaters reach temperature in about 30 to 45 minutes, give you precise control, and need a dedicated 240V circuit. Wood-burning stoves take longer to heat, run off-grid, and bring the atmosphere of a real fire. Both make steam when you pour water on the stones.

mainEntity.name: How much is delivery for a heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delivery for a heater bought on its own is quoted for your location, or you can pick it up free at our Schomberg showroom when in stock. If you buy a sauna from us, the heater is included in the sauna's delivery and installation.

mainEntity.name: What size breaker does a sauna heater need?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the heater and its output: from a 30 A double-pole breaker for 6 kW heaters like the HUUM Drop 6 kW or Harvia KIP 6 kW, up to 80 A for the Homecraft Apex 15 kW. The exact breaker and wire size for every output is listed on each heater page.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an electrician and a permit in Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An electric sauna heater must be connected by a licensed electrical contractor under an Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) permit, following the Ontario Electrical Safety Code.

mainEntity.name: Can I start my sauna from my phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a Wi-Fi control. HUUM heaters use the UKU Wi-Fi control, and Homecraft heaters can be paired with a Homecraft Wi-Fi touchpad. Both are available on our Accessories page.

mainEntity.name: Is there a difference between indoor and outdoor controls?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Homecraft heaters, yes: choose the outdoor contactor and touchpad for a backyard sauna, and the indoor version for a basement or home sauna.

mainEntity.name: Do wood-burning heaters need a chimney?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Wood-burning stoves need a chimney, installed to local building codes, on a non-combustible base with the clearances listed for each stove. Check your home insurer's requirements before installing a wood stove.

mainEntity.name: Are the electric heaters safety certified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Homecraft heaters (Revive, Revive Slim, Apex Mini and Apex) are CSA certified to UL 875, and the Harvia KIP is UL/cUL listed.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with each heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homecraft heaters carry a 2-year manufacturer warranty, HUUM heaters a 3-year warranty, the Harvia KIP up to 3 years, and Narvi stoves 2 years. Details are on each heater page.

Homecraft (Revive, Revive Slim, Apex Mini, Apex) and TimberGlow are made in Canada. Narvi stoves and the Harvia KIP come from Finland. HUUM heaters are designed in Estonia, and the Pellum pellet stove is designed and made there too.
